newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland takes part in "virtual" African University.
newsitem.headline: Ireland takes part in "virtual" African University.

text.p: Ireland on Wednesday formally joined a World Bank-funded project to set up a "Virtual University" by providing computer-based educational courses to African countries.

"The African Virtual University project will provide an appropriate 21st century high-technology expression for Ireland's traditional commitment to collaboration with Africa and its peoples," Minister of State for Commerce, Science and Technology Pat Rabbitte said.

The project, launched by United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Anan, will supply English and French-speaking sub-Saharan Africa with a range of courses in sciences, engineering, business and health care.
The English-language service will operate from the United States and Ireland. Its French counterpart will be beamed from France and Belgium.
An estimated two per cent of Africa's eligible population goes to University, compared with around 50 in the developed world.

"For over a year now, Irish agencies and institutions have worked to make this project a reality on the ground and as soon as the business of commissioning equipment on the ground in Africa is completed, test tranmsissions will start," Rabbitte said.
Ireland touts itself as the "Silicon Valley" of Europe because of the range and number of foreign computer companies which have set up offshoots across the country.
